title: Disjunction and admissible rules in intuitionistic propositional logic

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic (ILLC report PP-2006-25; ESSLLI 2005 lectures)
based_on.pages: Section 3.4 printed pp. 20–21: Theorem 17, Definition 24 and Example 25(1). The entry uses the corrected negated-antecedent rule noted in BDJ-IPC-01.

summary: Gluing ordered countermodels proves the disjunction property and separates substitution-admissible rules from rules derivable under an assumption.
abstract: An intuitionistic proof of a disjunction without assumptions guarantees that one disjunct has a proof. We establish this by placing two countermodels above a new common world, while preserving every formula at their old worlds. A shared negated assumption survives this construction too, yielding an independence-of-premise rule. The rule preserves theorems under every substitution, yet a four-world example shows that its conclusion cannot generally be deduced from its premise. This distinguishes admissibility from derivability and explains why the rule cannot simply be used inside arbitrary open proof branches.
